document.lead: You should spend about 20 minutes on this task.

text: The bar chart compares the percentage of adults aged 25–34 and 55–64 who had a university degree in five countries in 2019.

Overall, younger adults were much more likely than older adults to have a degree in every country. South Korea had the highest figure for young adults, while Italy and Mexico had the lowest figures for both age groups. The pattern was therefore similar in all five countries.

Among 25–34 year olds, 70% of South Koreans had a degree, followed by Canada at 66% and Japan at 61%. In contrast, only 28% of young Italians and 25% of young Mexicans had one. These two countries were far behind the other three. Japan's figure for young adults was nine points lower than that of South Korea.

The older groups had lower figures everywhere. Canada was highest at 33%, followed by Japan with 24%. The gap between the age groups was largest in South Korea, where the figure fell from 70% to just 13%. In Italy and Mexico, the older groups had only 11% and 10%, so the gap there was much smaller.
